title: City of Bakersfield introduces garden project in southeast to fight food scarcity - NewsBreak
text:
BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) — Food scarcity continues to be a persistent issue here in southeast Bakersfield. The city and some non-profits are looking into different ways to bring more food into the community — including, by putting a garden right here on Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard. A proposed agreement between the City of Bakersfield and Circle of Life Development Foundation’s MLK CommUNITY Garden Initiative could transform a vacant corner in southeast Bakersfield into a new community garden. With a budget of $728,904, the funding for this project comes from the $22 million grant designated for the Southeast Strong initiative, which aims to bring new affordable housing, urban greening, better public transportation and more.
Southeast Bakersfield residents are excited. “I’d like to see some collard greens, cucumbers, maybe tomatoes, and okra — that all sounds good to me,” said resident Wilma Russ. “What excites me about the garden is seeing the beauty, the scenery, the colors. Being born and raised over here, it’s like you kinda miss that — the colors,” said resident Lila Jennings. “If the people are growing it together, awesome. I mean, everybody gets to pitch in. Grow your own little garden. They might want to grow this, you might want to grow that, but it will benefit the people who don’t have anything,” said resident Vince Barnes. A Department of Agriculture study found that southeast Bakersfield, covering over 9,000 people and 2,300 households as of 2019, is a food desert due to its lower income and minimal access to supermarkets and large grocery stores. Other areas in Kern — like Lost Hills and Ridgecrest — are also considered to be food deserts. MLK ComUNITY’s Emprezz Nontzikelelo says that a new garden would both work to address food scarcity in southeast Bakersfield and create an enhanced sense of community.
“Without growing a community, we cannot grow a garden. We will be growing — along with that community — healthy food. Nutritious food. And beautifying — there will be plants and flowers and healing spaces, and all of the things that is going to renew — restore — reclaim this southeast community.” With city approval, this new garden could be a lifeline for those seeking new food options in this Southeast Bakersfield community.
